title: No-Setup Self-Working Card Trick: Four-of-a-Kind Reveal (Cross-Cut Force + Spelling)
summary: Matt McGurk presents a no-setup, self-working card trick in which the spectator shuffles the deck and a prediction card is introduced before the performance unfolds. The bottom card of the deck, revealed to the audience after a simple dealing-and-cross-cut setup, determines which four of a kind will appear at the end. The trick is built around a quick arrangement that puts three identical ranks into a stacked sequence, followed by a cross-cut force to reveal the first three cards, a spelling routine that asks the spectator to spell the rank (e.g., “three” or “nine”) as cards are dealt, and a final revelation where the fourth matching card appears from the magician’s hand. The performer emphasizes speed and visibility by handling the setup in front of the spectator and using misdirection to keep the process smooth. The technique is attributed to Larry Jennings, with McGurk presenting his streamlined version and a step-by-step explanation of how the deck is arranged and used to produce the four-of-a-kind reveal from a shuffled deck.

Revealing the three of a kind through spelling

sections.description: The presenter explains how the bottom card of the deck, when turned toward the performer, determines the four-of-a-kind. He details a rapid setup: compute the number of letters in the bottom-card rank, form a packet of five cards (three plus two fillers) for the first three, then place subsequent threes to create two more identical ranks, with a prediction card set aside for later revelation.

sections.description: The trick unfolds with the spectator cutting and the magician performing a cross-cut force to deliver the first three. The performer asks the spectator to spell the rank (e.g., 'three') as cards are dealt, keeping the hand as the working pile. The audience is guided to observe that the predicted card aligns with the revealed rank, and the final card shown from the magician’s hand completes the four-of-a-kind from the shuffled deck.

sections.title: Final Thoughts
sections.description: The host reiterates the effectiveness and speed of the setup, credits the original trick to Larry Jennings, and invites viewer engagement and subscription. The closing notes emphasize that this is among the best self-working tricks and encourage further exploration and discussion.
